# dsh-codex-login

DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin: sign in to **ChatGPT (Codex)** through the
official OAuth flow, so th

e pi-ai `openai-codex` provider's GPT models can be
used as the harness's **main model** — not just

i-codex` provider's GPT models can be
used as the harness's **main model** — not just as a subagent.
## Why this plugin exists
DSH ships two halves of the Codex sign-in story but no bridge between them:

- `dsh-llm-pi-ai` serves the pi-ai `openai-codex` catalog provider. That
provider is **OAuth-only**:

it authenticates through ChatGPT, and it has no
API-key method.
- The host mounts `dsh-authorizatio

n`, and pi-ai registers its
"Sign in with ChatGPT" flow on that seam when `llm-pi-ai` mounts.
- The

bundled web client exposes **no authorization RPC** (only
`credentials/describe|set|unset`), so no b
undled UI can start that flow.

This plugin drives the same official seam from the host plane and surfaces it
as an agent tool. The

flow itself — PKCE, the browser redirect to
`http://localhost:1455/auth/callback`, the token exchang

e, the credential
commit and the cross-process refresh lock — is entirely pi-ai's own
implementation
. The plugin only starts it and relays notices/prompts.
## Tool
| Tool | Actions |
| `codex_login` | `start` (default) — start the flow and return the browser URL; `status` — progress
+ credential state; `submit_code` — paste the final callback URL/code, or answer pi-ai's login-meth
od prompt with `browser` / `device_code`; `cancel` — withdraw the attempt |

`start` begins the attempt in the background and returns as soon as the
authorization URL (or the lo

gin-method prompt) is available. Complete the
login in the browser; the credential is committed auto

prompt) is available. Complete the
login in the browser; the credential is committed automatically.
## Where the credential goes
The flow commits one record into the harness credential store:

- key: `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex`
- kind: `grant`, payload `{ type, access, refresh, expires, accountI

y: `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex`
- kind: `grant`, payload `{ type, access, refresh, expires, accountId }`

The plugin never prints, logs, or re-emits any credential material. Tokens are
refreshed by pi-ai un
der its own cross-process lock.
## Model catalog
Keep the provider entry empty:

An empty provider inherits the app's built-in pi-ai catalog — every model the
installed build suppor

ts, with **new models appearing automatically after app
updates**. Writing a `models:` list *replace

s* that catalog (models are then
limited to the list and never auto-update); use `modelOverrides` to

tweak a
single catalog model instead.
## Install (desktop app profile)

1. Put this package at `~/.dsh/profiles/packages/dsh-codex-login/`
2. In `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/pa

ckage.json` add
`"dsh-codex-login": "link:/Users/<you>/.dsh/profiles/packages/dsh-codex-login"`
and

append `"dsh-codex-login"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`
3. Install dependencies with the app's bundled p

npm, then **restart the app**
4. Ask the agent to sign in; or drive the tool directly
Profiles are managed by the Electron app: the CLI refuses `--profile desktop`.
## Requirements

- DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 (any profile that mounts `dsh-authorization`, `dsh-credentials`
and `dsh-llm-pi-ai`

)
- A ChatGPT account with Codex access; model availability follows your plan
## Notes

- The OAuth callback binds `127.0.0.1:1455`; the browser must run on the same
machine as the harness

.
- One attempt per credential at a time (enforced by `dsh-authorization`).
- If the browser callbac

k cannot reach the harness, copy the final
`http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?code=…` URL back wit

he harness, copy the final
`http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?code=…` URL back with `submit_code`.
